commitResults.messageTitle: Add Note class for candidate notes
commitResults.messageBody:
Recruiters need to keep recruitment and interview information with
each candidate, but Person has no field for free-form text.

Let's add a Note value class for later commits to attach to Person.
Unlike Address, Note accepts any text, including an empty string, so
notes stay optional and recruiters are not blocked by format rules
on what is meant to be free-form information.

Recruiters need notes on each candidate, and Note exists but is not
yet part of Person.

Let's add a note field to Person and pass a note at every place that
creates one. EditCommand carries the existing note over, so editing
another field does not wipe it. AddCommandParser, JsonAdaptedPerson
and SampleDataUtil pass an empty note until later commits let users
enter, save and see notes.

Notes are left out of isSamePerson, as two records with the same name
are the same candidate regardless of their notes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save candidate notes to the data file
commitResults.messageBody:
Notes are part of Person, but JsonAdaptedPerson does not save them,
so any note would be lost when the app restarts.

Let's add a note field to JsonAdaptedPerson so notes are written to
and read from the data file. A missing note loads as an empty note
rather than an error, so data files saved before notes existed still
load.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show candidate notes in the UI and messages
commitResults.messageBody:
Notes are saved with each candidate but are not shown anywhere, so
users cannot read the notes they record.

Let's show the note on the candidate card, below the email, and
include it in the message shown after add, delete and edit. The note
wraps so long notes stay readable, and is hidden when empty so cards
without notes look the same as before. Give some sample candidates
notes so new users can see what notes are for.

The card's grid column prefers a width of 150px, and JavaFX uses that
width to work out the card's height. A wrapped note then reserves
room for more lines than it needs, leaving an empty gap at the bottom
of the card. Drop that preferred width and keep each list cell as
wide as the list. As a side effect, cards with many tags also lose
the same empty gap.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add nt/ prefix for notes in add command
commitResults.messageBody:
Candidates can have notes, but the add command has no way to set one,
so every candidate added through the app ends up with an empty note.

Let's accept an optional nt/NOTE in the add command, so a recruiter
can record details such as an interview date when adding a candidate.
As with the other single-valued fields, a repeated nt/ is rejected.

A note cannot contain a space followed by a prefix such as t/ or n/,
as the tokenizer starts a new field there. Supporting that would need
an escape syntax, which is more than the MVP needs, so tests pin down
the behaviour instead to make any later change to it deliberate.

Editing notes and documenting nt/ in the User Guide are left to
separate changes.

Person#hashCode includes the note, but no test calls it, so a
change that drops the note from the hash goes unnoticed. Java
collections such as HashSet rely on equal persons having equal hash
codes, so hashCode must stay consistent with equals, which already
compares notes.

Let's check that equal persons share a hash code and that persons
differing only in their note get different hash codes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove nt/ prefix from add command
commitResults.messageBody:
The add command accepts an optional nt/NOTE, but the tokenizer ends
the note at the next recognized prefix. "nt/Discuss t/java" is saved
as the note "Discuss" plus a java tag, and "nt/Referee: n/Alice" is
rejected as a duplicate name, so valid notes are silently changed or
refused.

Notes are meant to be recorded on an existing candidate, usually
after an interview (UC06), which the add command cannot do anyway.

Let's remove nt/ from the add command, so new candidates start with
an empty note. A separate note command will set notes instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add note command to record candidate notes
commitResults.messageBody:
Candidates can have notes, but there is no command to set or change
a note once the candidate has been added.

Let's add `note INDEX NOTE`, which replaces the note of the candidate
at INDEX, or clears it when NOTE is empty.

Taking everything after the index as the note lets a note hold any
text, so it avoids the misparsed notes that nt/ in the add command
produced. The User Guide documents the new command.

Some note command behaviour from issue #42 is untested or tested only
indirectly:

* The AddressBookParser test uses a plain note, so prefix-like text
  such as "t/" is checked only by NoteCommandParser, not after
  AddressBookParser splits off the command word.
* The "Call back" case in the invalid index test repeats the
  non-numeric index case, so it adds no coverage.
* Clearing the note of a person who has no note is untested.

Let's,
* use a note containing "t/" and "n/" in the AddressBookParser test
* replace the repeated case with "1Call back", a note joined to the
  index without a space
* check that clearing an empty note leaves the person unchanged and
  reports the note as cleared
Add notes to candidates

Candidates have no record of which role opening they are applying
for, so a recruiter cannot tell which candidates belong to which
role.

Let's give every candidate a required role title:

* add requires r/ROLE and saves the title with the candidate
* edit, note and status keep the candidate's existing role
* edit rejects r/, so it is not silently read as part of another
  field's value, until changing a role is supported
* a saved candidate with a missing or invalid role is invalid data

A missing role is rejected rather than defaulted, as there is no role
every candidate could sensibly fall back to. Data files saved before
this change therefore fail to load.

Checking that the role exists and is open is left to a later commit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject candidates for missing or closed roles
commitResults.messageBody:
A candidate's role title is checked only for its format, so a
candidate can be added to a role that does not exist or whose hiring
has finished.

Let's check the role against the roles in RecruiterBuddy:

* add rejects a role that does not exist or is closed
* add saves the role's own spelling of the title, so r/software
  engineer is saved as Software Engineer
* loading rejects a saved candidate whose role is not in the roles
  list, but accepts one whose role is closed, as closing a role keeps
  its candidates

Roles are matched ignoring case, as role titles are already unique
ignoring case.

The sample data gains the roles of the sample candidates, so that it
satisfies the same rule.

commitResults.messageTitle: Docs: Require launching from the JAR folder
commitResults.messageBody:
RecruiterBuddy resolves its data, preferences and log file paths
against the working directory. Launching it from another folder, such
as by double-clicking the JAR on some systems, makes it read and write
those files outside the JAR's folder. This breaks the course's
Constraint-Data-Sandbox. The DG manual tests also tell testers to
double-click the JAR, which can make them misreport saving as broken.

Let's document the required launch method until the paths are fixed
in code:

* Quick Start: warn to always launch from a terminal in the JAR's
  folder
* Data file section: state that the file is saved relative to the
  launch folder and created after the first successful command
* FAQ: replace the AB3 "home folder" wording
* Known issues: describe the wrong-folder symptom and a recovery that
  backs up both data files before choosing one
* DG launch tests: run the JAR from a terminal instead of
  double-clicking, and expect only preferences.json and addressbook.log
  on first launch

This is a workaround, not full compliance, since the app can still
access files elsewhere if launched differently.

Configuration.md describes a config.json file that controls the log
level and the preferences file location. AB3 removed that support,
so the app ignores config.json, and no page links to the guide. The
site map's "Documentation, logging, testing, configuration, dev-ops"
link also points to an anchor that does not exist, as the DG heading
has no "configuration".

Let's delete the guide and point the site map link to the DG's
"Documentation, logging, testing, dev-ops" heading. The Logging guide
already explains how to change the log level.
Align docs with v1.3 behaviour before release

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Interview class for interview dates and times
commitResults.messageBody:
Candidates have no way to record an interview slot, so recruiters
type it into the note, where a mistyped or impossible date goes
unnoticed.

Let's add an Interview value class that accepts only zero-padded
YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM values that are real dates and 24-hour times, and
an Interview.NONE value for candidates with no interview.

Format errors and impossible values get separate messages, as PE
testers treat calling an invalid value a format error as a bug.
ParserUtil.parseInterview exposes both checks for the upcoming
interview command and for loading saved data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Person: Add interview field and save it to storage
commitResults.messageBody:
Candidates need an interview date and time that the card, storage
and the upcoming interview command can rely on.

Let's add an Interview field to Person, defaulting to Interview.NONE,
and save it in the data file. A missing or empty interview loads as
no interview, so files saved by v1.3 still load.

Every command that rebuilds a Person (note, status, edit, and role
changes) now copies the interview, so updating another field never
wipes it. The sample data moves Alex Yeoh's interview out of the note
into the new field, and mixes candidates with and without interviews
so both card states are visible.

Saved interviews are not visible anywhere, so recruiters cannot see
when a candidate's interview is.

Let's show the interview on the candidate card as
"Interview: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM", in the same form users type it, and
hide the line for candidates with no interview so their cards have no
blank row. Command results that list a candidate's details now
include the interview as well.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add interview command to schedule interviews
commitResults.messageBody:
Recruiters can see a candidate's interview but have no command to
set it.

Let's add "interview INDEX d/YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM" to schedule or replace
an interview, and "interview INDEX" to clear it. Results name the
updated candidate, so recruiters can tell who changed when working
through a filtered list.

An empty d/ is rejected instead of clearing the interview, so a
mistyped date never wipes an existing one. Clearing a candidate with
no interview, or repeating the same date, still succeeds, as with
note. The command keeps the current filter, which the planned
find-and-update workflow relies on.

The guide tells users to type interview dates into notes, where
nothing checks them, and does not mention the interview command.

Let's add an interview section with the date rules, how to clear an
interview, and examples, worded to match the error messages. Point
note users to interview for dates, describe the interview field in
the data file section, and add the command to the summary table.

The guide describes notes as the place for interview dates, has no
section on how interviews are implemented, and UC04 promises
interviewer and location details that the product does not record.

Let's add a "Candidate interviews" implementation section covering
validation, the command, storage, and the main design decisions.
Update UC04 to match the command, including clearing and the two
kinds of invalid date, and replace the interview-style note examples
in manual testing. Add manual tests for scheduling, rejecting
invalid dates, keeping the filter, and saving interviews.

commitResults.messageTitle: UserGuide: State what interview does when nothing changes
commitResults.messageBody:
The guide says clearing an empty interview or repeating the same date
"changes nothing", which a reader could take to mean the command is
ignored or shows a different message.

State instead that such commands still succeed with the usual result
message and leave the candidate unchanged, so the guide describes
exactly what users will see.

commitResults.messageTitle: NoteCommand: Name the candidate in the result message
commitResults.messageBody:
The note result message prints every field of the updated candidate.
The result box shows only the start of that line, so a recruiter
working through a filtered list cannot easily tell whose note changed
or what was saved.

Let's shorten the message to the candidate's name and the new note,
or the name alone when the note is cleared, so the important part
fits in the result box.

Also add an assertion that the edited candidate holds the new note,
and log each note change to help trace issues.

commitResults.messageTitle: SampleDataUtil: Vary candidate statuses and add a closed role
commitResults.messageBody:
Every sample candidate starts at Pending Resume Screening and every
sample role is open. A first-time user therefore cannot see what the
other statuses or a closed role look like.

Let's give the sample candidates a mix of statuses that covers every
status, and add a closed UX Designer role. The closed role's
candidates all have final outcomes and no role has more than one hired
candidate, so the data obeys the rules that the status and role close
commands enforce. Also replace the leftover AB3 tags, such as friends
and family, with recruiting tags.

Remove the test that expects every sample candidate to have the
default status, as it no longer holds. Update the Developer Guide's
manual test prerequisite to list the closed role.

commitResults.messageTitle: SampleDataUtil: Avoid UG example phone and stale date
commitResults.messageBody:
Nur Aisyah's phone matches the phone in the User Guide's add example,
so that example will be rejected as a duplicate once candidates are
compared by phone. Alex Yeoh's note also gives an interview date that
will be in the past when testers use the app.

Let's give Nur Aisyah an unused phone number and drop the date from
Alex Yeoh's note.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update name and phone validation rules
commitResults.messageBody:
Names allow only ASCII letters, digits and spaces, so real names such
as O'Brien, Tan, Mei Ling or Ravi s/o Kumar are rejected. Phones accept
any 3 or more digits, so numbers that cannot be real are accepted.

Let's make names 1 to 100 characters long, starting with a letter in
any language, and allow digits, spaces and ' - . , / ( ) after it.
Accent marks are allowed too, as an accented letter can be typed as a
plain letter followed by a separate mark.

Let's make phones 8 to 15 digits with an optional leading +, allowing
single spaces or hyphens between digits. Phone stores the number
without separators, so differently formatted inputs of the same number
are equal and the data file holds one canonical form.

Update the User Guide with both rules and a tip to write a/l and a/p
as A/L and A/P, since a/ starts the address. Pad the 7-digit phones in
the test data so it satisfies the new phone rule.

commitResults.messageTitle: Ignore phone separators and clarify UG field rules
commitResults.messageBody:
Phones accept only single spaces or hyphens between digits, so common
inputs such as 9123 - 4567 or + 65 9123 4567 are rejected even though
their digits are valid. The UG states the name and phone rules as long
sentences placed between the ROLE notes, which makes them hard to find
and scan.

Let's ignore all spaces and hyphens in phones and check only for an
optional leading + and 8 to 15 digits. The digit count and the +
position are what make a number valid; the separators carry no
meaning, and they are removed when saved anyway.

Let's also list the name and phone rules as short bullets in parameter
order, describing what is accepted rather than giving orders, and word
the error messages the same way. Use PHONE_NUMBER consistently in the
edit command format.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add defensive checks to Name and Phone
commitResults.messageBody:
Name.isValidName and Phone.isValidPhone reject a null argument only
indirectly, through the NullPointerException of the first method call
on it. The Phone constructor assumes that removing separators from a
valid phone always leaves an optional + followed by digits, but
nothing checks this.

Let's state the non-null contract with requireNonNull, so a null
fails fast at the method boundary, and assert the stored phone's form
so that a future change to separator removal that breaks it is caught
during development.

commitResults.messageTitle: Detect duplicate candidates by email or phone
commitResults.messageBody:
Candidates are treated as duplicates when their names match. This
blocks different people who share a name, while letting the same
person be added twice under another spelling of their name.

Let's treat two candidates as duplicates when their emails match,
ignoring case, or their phone numbers match. Names may now repeat.
Phone numbers are compared as saved, so a number with and without
its country code count as different; the User Guide documents this.

add and edit name the existing candidate and the clashing field.
edit excludes the candidate being edited, so keeping their own email
does not hide a clash with another candidate's phone number. The
same rule applies when loading the data file.

# Conflicts:
#	docs/UserGuide.md
#	src/main/java/seedu/address/logic/commands/EditCommand.java
Name the updated candidate in the note result message

# Conflicts:
#	docs/UserGuide.md

commitResults.messageTitle: Phone: Remove redundant assert on stored value
commitResults.messageBody:
The Phone constructor asserts that the stored value matches
VALIDATION_REGEX right after checkArgument has validated the same
separator-stripped string against the same regex. The assert can
never fail, and its unreachable failure branch leaves the line
partially covered, dropping patch coverage below the Codecov target.

Let's remove the assert. The constructor still rejects invalid input
through checkArgument, so the stored value is guaranteed to be valid.

commitResults.messageTitle: Log rejected duplicates and clarify duplicate messages
commitResults.messageBody:
A rejected duplicate add or edit leaves no trace in the log beyond
the command text, so the reason for the rejection is lost. The data
file error says only "duplicate person(s)", which does not say what
makes two candidates duplicates.

Let's log each rejected add or edit with the clashing candidate and
field, as #87 asks. The data file error now names the email and
phone rule, and the duplicate message helper rejects null arguments
before its assertion runs.

The User Guide example now uses +6591234567, which needs the phone
format from #82, so this branch should be merged after #82.

master adds editing a candidate's role, renaming roles and backing up
unreadable data files. Both sides changed EditCommand and the User
Guide's edit and data file sections.

Keep master's role-edit messages and drop its generic duplicate
message, which the email and phone messages replace. Add the
duplicate rule to master's new edit and data file text.

master's new tests build candidates that differ only by name, which
now clash by email or phone. Give them distinct contact details, and
check a clashing email instead of a shared name during a transfer.

Master and this branch both change NoteCommand: master adds an assert
and names the candidate in the success message, while this branch
passes the new interview field through when rebuilding the Person.

Keep both changes in NoteCommand, and update the interview-preserving
NoteCommandTest case to expect master's new message format so it no
longer fails with a missing format argument.
Update name and phone validation

Master adds name and phone validation rules (#112), including a User
Guide bullet on candidate fields in the data file. This branch adds a
bullet on duplicate emails and phones to the same list, so the two
edits conflict.

Keep both bullets in a single list, with master's name and phone rules
first, so the data-file section documents every constraint the loader
enforces.
Detect duplicate candidates by email or phone
Add interview command to schedule candidate interviews

commitResults.messageTitle: DeveloperGuide: Add candidate and interview diagrams
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG describes a candidate's fields and the interview command only
in text. The model class diagram omits candidate fields, so readers
cannot see how a candidate holds its role, note, status and interview,
or how interview INDEX clears an interview.

Let's add a candidate class diagram showing each field with its
implemented multiplicity, and an interview sequence diagram covering
parsing, date and time validation, the displayed-candidate lookup, the
model update and saving. Interview and Status use plain associations,
as Interview.NONE and the status constants are shared by candidates.

The DG text now states that scheduling another interview replaces the
previous one.

The interview sequence diagram draws the argument tokenizer, the
argument multimap and the role-list guard as separate calls. These
are shared by every command or matter only when they fail, so they
lengthen the diagram without explaining the interview feature.

Let's describe them in notes instead, keeping the calls for parsing,
date and time validation, lookup, replacement, model update and
saving.

The candidate class diagram also shows member visibility as
PlantUML icons, which readers may not recognise. Show the UML
symbols + and - instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix build broken by merging #122 and #123
commitResults.messageBody:
Each PR passes CI on its own, but master fails after both are merged.
Both add a logger field to EditCommand, so EditCommand declares
logger twice and does not compile. A new diagnostics test from #122
also adds a candidate that differs from another only by name, which
#123's email-or-phone rule treats as a duplicate.

Let's remove the second logger declaration, and give the test's
second candidate its own email and phone, as other tests already do
since #123.
Fix build broken by merging #122 and #123
Add UML diagrams for candidate structure and interviews

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept standard email symbols and warn on dotless domains
commitResults.messageBody:
The email rule allows only + _ . - before the @, and never two of
them in a row. Valid addresses such as o'brien@example.com and
a._a@example.com are rejected, while a likely typo such as
john@gmailcom is saved silently. The error message lists the allowed
symbols but not the adjacency rule, so users cannot tell why an
address is rejected.

Let's accept the unquoted local-part form of RFC 5322, which is also
what the HTML standard accepts for email inputs, so no address that a
provider issues is rejected. Quoted local parts stay unsupported, as
their spaces could be read as command prefixes.

A domain without a dot is valid, so add and edit still save it, but
append a warning to the success message. Edit warns only when the
email changes, so editing other fields does not repeat it.

Rewrite the error message to state the rules in plain words, and
document the rules in the UG and the design choices in the DG.

Fixes #146

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn when an email has unusual symbols
commitResults.messageBody:
Emails may now contain any symbol that RFC 5322 allows before the @.
Most of these symbols, such as # or !, never appear in addresses that
email providers issue, so an email that has one is most likely a typo
and is saved without any notice.

Let's warn, without blocking, when the part before the @ has a symbol
other than . _ - + ', the symbols that major providers issue. Each
unusual symbol is named once in the warning, so the user can spot the
typo. The warning joins the existing dotless-domain warning in the
add and edit success messages, and follows the same rule of appearing
in edit only when the email changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the specific problem in email error messages
commitResults.messageBody:
Every invalid email gets the same message listing all the rules, so a
user who types john..doe@example.com or a stray comma has to work out
which rule they broke. The domain rule also rejects consecutive
hyphens inside a domain part, so encoded non-English domains such as
xn--80ak6aa92e.com are refused although they are valid host names.

Let's check emails in a fixed order and report only the first
problem, naming any invalid character and whether it is before or
after the @. Related problems share one short message where the cause
is easy to spot, such as a misplaced dot before the @, which keeps
the number of messages small.

The checker replaces the email regex, so the messages cannot disagree
with what is rejected. Storage uses the same messages, which helps
when the data file is edited by hand. Domain parts may now contain
consecutive hyphens, as host names allow.

The note command resets the list to show all candidates after saving
a note, while the interview command keeps the current filter. After
a find, the displayed numbers shift, so a recruiter adding notes to a
filtered list can put the next note on the wrong candidate.

Let's keep the filter, as interview does. A note does not affect
which candidates match a filter, so the edited candidate stays in the
displayed list.

Update the User Guide, the Developer Guide and its manual test to
state that the filtered list stays filtered.

commitResults.messageTitle: NoteCommand: Suggest undo when a note is replaced or cleared
commitResults.messageBody:
A new note replaces the existing one without saying so, and clearing
a note does not show what was removed. A user who means to add to a
note, or who presses Enter too early, loses the previous note without
noticing that undo can restore it.

Let's say when a note is replaced or cleared, and suggest undo in
both cases. Clearing also shows the cleared note, since the user
cannot see it anywhere else. Replacing does not repeat the old note,
which may be long. When nothing is lost, the message has no hint.

The candidate's name and the hint come first and the note comes
last, so a long note cannot push them out of the result box.

commitResults.messageTitle: Stop suggesting that notes hold interview details
commitResults.messageBody:
The note command's usage example is "note 1 Interview 2026-10-20
14:00", and the first sample candidate's note is "Interview with the
hiring manager". Both suggest recording interviews in notes, while the
User Guide says to use the interview command, which checks the date
and shows it on the card.

Let's use examples that show what notes are for, such as a
candidate's skills and availability, so users are not steered
towards keeping interview details as unchecked free text.

The candidate card shows the role as "Applying for: ..." and the
interview as "Interview: ...", but shows the note as plain text. A
note such as "9123 4567 (mum)" can then be mistaken for the
candidate's own phone number or address.

Let's show the note as "Note: ...", matching the other labelled
lines, and mention the label in the User Guide and Developer Guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Docs: State what notes do not support yet
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide does not say that notes cannot be added to, cannot
hold line breaks, and are not searched by find. Users who try these
learn the limits only by trial, and the Developer Guide does not
record why notes are replaced rather than added to.

Let's list these limits in a "Not supported in this version" box,
with an example of extending a note by retyping it. Let's also add a
design consideration explaining that adding to a note needs its own
command word, because a marker such as a leading "+" would clash with
notes that start with it, so it is planned for a future version.

commitResults.messageTitle: DeveloperGuide: Align note requirements with replace-only notes
commitResults.messageBody:
The main note user story says notes retain interview information,
although interviews have their own command. UC06 is titled "Add
Candidate Notes" and says the note is added, which suggests that a
new note is appended, while the note command replaces the existing
note. It also refers to several notes, although each candidate has
one.

Let's describe notes as holding details such as skills and
availability, and rename UC06 to "Set or Clear a Candidate's Note".
Its steps now say the note is saved, and new extensions cover
replacing a different note, clearing a note, and clearing when there
is no note, matching the command's behaviour.

The interview sequence diagram says the command is rejected when the
role list is shown, but both lists are always shown and the check no
longer exists. The note usage example records an interview time,
while the User Guide tells users to use the interview command, which
checks the date and time.

Let's drop the role-list check from the diagram note, and give note
an example that is not an interview time.

commitResults.messageTitle: interview: Explain mistakes and warn on unusual interviews
commitResults.messageBody:
Every index mistake in interview shows "Invalid command format!", so
a user cannot tell whether the index is missing, is not a number, is
past the end of the list, or is followed by stray text. Interviews
that are likely mistakes, such as a mistyped year, a candidate who is
already rejected, or two candidates at the same time, are saved
without comment.

Let's give each index mistake its own message, and add a line to the
result message for each likely mistake. The interview is still saved,
because each case can be legitimate, such as a panel interviewing two
candidates at once.

Today's date comes from a Clock, so tests can fix it. The success
messages also end with a full stop, like the note messages.

commitResults.messageTitle: UserGuide: State that sorting by interview date is not supported
commitResults.messageBody:
The interview section does not say whether candidates can be sorted or
filtered by interview date. The Developer Guide lists both as user
stories, so a reader may expect them, and the UG gives no hint that
they are missing.

Let's state in the interview section that both are planned for a
future version, so readers are not left searching for them.

commitResults.messageTitle: UserGuide: Fix broken link to the status command
commitResults.messageBody:
The interview section links to the status command with the anchor
#updating-a-candidates-status-status, but MarkBind turns the
apostrophe in "candidate's" into a hyphen, so the link goes nowhere.

Let's use the anchor that MarkBind generates for that heading.

commitResults.messageTitle: DeveloperGuide: Add interview warnings to UC04
commitResults.messageBody:
The interview command warns about interviews that might be mistakes,
but UC04 does not mention this, so the use case leaves out a path
that users see.

Let's add an extension in which RecruiterBuddy records such an
interview and points out each possible mistake.

commitResults.messageTitle: interview: Show the status note first and shorten it
commitResults.messageBody:
When an interview gets several notes, the far-future year reminder
comes before the note that the candidate already has a final status.
The status note is the stronger signal, as the interview may not be
needed at all. It is also the longest line, at about 120 characters,
which can be cut off in the result box.

Let's show the status note first and reduce it to the candidate's
name and status. The User Guide keeps the advice to update the
status, so the message does not need to repeat it.

commitResults.messageTitle: interview: Skip the status note for past interviews
commitResults.messageBody:
Recording a past interview for a candidate with a final outcome adds
a note about their status. The User Guide accepts past dates so that
recruiters can record interviews that already happened, so for a
rejected or hired candidate the note is a false alarm.

Let's add the note only when the interview is today or later.

The Developer Guide test case for the note uses a fixed date that
will soon be in the past, so it now uses any date after today.

commitResults.messageTitle: UserGuide: Stop promising the usual interview result message
commitResults.messageBody:
The interview section says that re-entering the same date and time
shows the usual result message. When the candidate has a final status
or shares the slot with another candidate, the message also has a
note about this, so the promise is not always kept.

Let's only say that the command succeeds and the candidate's details
stay the same. The notes are explained in a later bullet.

commitResults.messageTitle: UserGuide: Explain that duplicate tags are saved once
commitResults.messageBody:
Typing the same tag twice, such as `t/test t/test`, shows only one tag
on the candidate card. The User Guide does not mention this, so users
may think a tag was lost.

Let's state in the add and edit sections that a repeated tag with the
same capitalisation is saved only once. The wording keeps the
capitalisation condition because tags are case-sensitive, so
`t/Java t/java` keeps both tags.

Closes #148.

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn on unusual or possibly duplicate phones
commitResults.messageBody:
add accepts any phone number with 8 to 15 digits, and rejects only
numbers that exactly match another candidate's. A number such as
12345678, which is not a Singapore number, is saved without comment
(#154). The numbers +65 9123 4567 and 91234567 are saved for two
candidates with no hint that they may be the same person.

Rejecting such numbers would also block real numbers, such as an
overseas number typed without its country code. The course treats
this as overzealous validation and prefers warning to blocking.

Let's accept these numbers, but add a note to the add and edit
result:

* a number treated as a Singapore number that does not have 8 digits
  starting with 3, 6, 8 or 9
* a number that differs from other candidates' numbers only by a + or
  the Singapore code 65, naming those candidates

Exact duplicates are still rejected. The data file loader keeps the
exact rule, so candidates accepted with a note can always be saved
and loaded again.

Also correct a DG manual test that expected a repeated name to be
rejected, as names may repeat.

Fixes #154

The note shown when a number does not look like a Singapore number
spans two long sentences and a full example number. In the result
box it wraps across several lines and buries the success message.

Let's cut it to one short line that still names the assumption and
the fix, adding the country code, so the user can act on it at a
glance.

Interview warnings can fill the fixed-height result display when many
candidates share a slot, while past dates receive no indication that the
year may be mistyped.

Warn about past dates, shorten status and distant-date messages, and
limit same-time details to two shortened names plus a remaining count.
Document the behavior and cover the new boundaries in command tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: NoteCommand: Shorten messages for adding and replacing a note
commitResults.messageBody:
Adding or replacing a note repeats the whole new note in the result
box, which already shows on the candidate's card. The result box does
not wrap, so a long note runs off the side. The replace message also
suggests undo, which makes it longer than needed.

Let's show one line naming the candidate instead, with a different
verb for adding, replacing and setting the same note again. Replacing
still says so, so an existing note is never overwritten silently,
while the User Guide explains that undo restores it. Clearing keeps
its undo hint and the cleared note, since nothing else shows it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn on edit only when the phone changes
commitResults.messageBody:
edit adds the phone number notes whenever p/ is given. Entering a
candidate's own number again, such as edit 1 p/12345678 when that is
already saved, repeats a note the user saw when the number was saved.

Let's add the notes only when the saved number differs from the old
one. A number that differs only by spaces or hyphens is saved the
same way, so it does not count as a change.

commitResults.messageTitle: UserGuide: Say emails, not addresses, in EMAIL notes
commitResults.messageBody:
The EMAIL notes in the add command say unsupported "addresses" have
spaces, quotation marks or non-English letters. Since the same command
also has an ADDRESS field, readers may think the note is about
ADDRESS.

Let's say "emails" instead, so the note clearly refers to EMAIL.
Add candidate: duplicate tag is ignored
interview: Fix interview bugs found
Warn on unusual or possibly duplicate phones

The phone warnings from #186 and the email warnings on this branch
both append to the add and edit success messages, so the two
branches conflict in AddCommand, EditCommand and Messages, and in
the field rules of the user and developer guides.

Keep both features: AddCommand appends phone and then email
warnings, and EditCommand checks each field only when it changes.
Keep both the email and phone sections in the guides.

commitResults.messageTitle: Email: Name validation methods and messages clearly
commitResults.messageBody:
Email#findProblem and its helpers return an error message, but
"problem" does not say what kind of value they return. The invalid
character message also builds its sentence from the words "before"
and "after", which callers pass in as plain strings.

Let's rename the methods to findValidationError, findLocalPartError
and findDomainError, and split the message into
MESSAGE_INVALID_LOCAL_PART_CHARACTER and
MESSAGE_INVALID_DOMAIN_CHARACTER, so each message is a complete
sentence that can be read and searched for as a whole.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move email warnings into EmailChecks and log all warnings
commitResults.messageBody:
Phone warnings live in PhoneChecks, but email warnings live in
Messages#appendEmailWarnings, so the two kinds of warnings are found
and appended in different places and in different ways. The end of
EditCommand#execute also mixes building the success message with
deciding which fields to check. None of the warnings is logged, and
a successful add is not logged either.

Let's add EmailChecks next to PhoneChecks, and let both append their
warnings through a shared Messages#appendWarnings. Let's move the
check for changed fields in EditCommand into its own method, and log
each warning and each added candidate, so the log shows why a
result message has extra lines.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use one Warning: prefix for all result warnings
commitResults.messageBody:
Phone and interview warnings start with "Note:", while email
warnings start with "Warning:". "Note" already means the candidate's
note, which the result message and the candidate card both label
"Note:", so a warning line can be mistaken for part of the note.

Let's start every phone, email and interview warning with
"Warning:", matching the names the code already uses for them, and
say "warning" instead of "note" for them in the guides. The
same-time interview line is a reminder rather than a warning, so it
keeps its "Also at this time:" wording.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove duplicated setup from warning tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The phone and email warning tests in AddCommandTest and
EditCommandTest each repeat the same steps to build the command, the
expected message and the expected model, and differ only in the
candidate and the warning lines. The repetition hides what each test
checks, and a change to the message format must be repeated in
every test.

Let's add assertAddSuccess and assertEditSuccess helpers that take
the expected warnings, so each test states only its inputs and
expected warnings. Let's also add a test that editing both the phone
and the email shows both warnings, since EditCommand now checks the
two fields separately.

commitResults.messageTitle: JsonAdaptedPerson: Convert each field in its own method
commitResults.messageBody:
toModelType checks name, phone, email and address inline, but hands
role, interview and status to helper methods, so it mixes two levels
of abstraction. The same missing-field check is also repeated for
each required field.

Let's give each field its own toModelX method and share the
missing-field check through requireField, so toModelType reads as a
list of the fields it converts.

the other field's error is now reported first, because tags are

commitResults.messageTitle: Move duplicate checks out of add and edit execute methods
commitResults.messageBody:
AddCommand#execute and EditCommand#execute each run the duplicate
email and phone check inline, next to role checks and saving, so
both methods mix the detailed check with the high-level steps of
the command.

Let's move each check into a verifyNotDuplicate method, so execute
reads as a list of steps. The two checks stay separate, because
editing must exclude the candidate being edited while adding must
not.

The tag changes from Micah turn the phone rules in the user guide's
"Adding a candidate" section into bullet points and add a TAG
section, while this branch adds an EMAIL section and calls the
phone note a warning, so the two edits conflict.

Keep the bullet format and the TAG section, add the EMAIL section
between the phone and tag rules, and say "warning" for the unusual
phone number. Fix "Without no country code" to "A number without a
country code" in the same line.

commitResults.messageTitle: AddCommand: Append warnings in a separate method
commitResults.messageBody:
AddCommand#execute chains the phone and email checks inline, and logs
the added candidate between building the message and appending the
warnings. EditCommand already appends its warnings through a helper,
so the two commands read differently.

Let's log right after the candidate is added, and move the warning
chain into appendWarnings, so execute reads as a list of steps like
EditCommand#execute.

commitResults.messageTitle: Email: Name the domain part rule and assert a single @
commitResults.messageBody:
findDomainError checks each domain part with an inline three-part
condition, which is more detailed than the lines around it.

exactly one @ with a name before it, but nothing states that.

Let's name the rule isValidDomainPart, like hasMisplacedDot in
findLocalPartError, and find the @ through getAtSignIndex, which
asserts that a valid email has exactly one @ after its name.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix coding standard violations in own code
commitResults.messageBody:
Some names do not match what they hold. A count is named like a
collection (otherCandidates), a method returning a warning is named
after candidates (findSameTimeCandidates), and single joined strings
have plural names that suggest a list. NoteCommandParser also has no
blank line before @throws and declares its index before assigning it
in a try block. Many lines go past the 110-character soft limit.

These are coding standard violations that checkstyle does not catch.

Let's,
* rename them to otherCandidateCount, findSameTimeWarning and
  ...Text names for joined strings
* move the index parsing into a helper so the variable is
  initialized where it is declared
* wrap every line over 110 characters, keeping all messages
  unchanged

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove duplicated code in note and interview code
commitResults.messageBody:
NoteCommand builds the edited candidate by copying every Person field
by hand, although Person offers withRole and withInterview for this.
A new Person field would have to be added to that copy too, or be lost
when a note is set.

InterviewCommandTest and NoteCommandTest repeat the same setup,
expected-model and assertion steps in most of their success tests, and
three EditCommandTest tests do so too, instead of using the helpers in
the same file.

Let's,
* add Person#withNote and use it in NoteCommand
* move replacePerson and copyModelWithPersonReplaced into

the filtered-list tests no longer set up the expected filter by hand.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove repeated empty note and interview checks
commitResults.messageBody:
An empty note is written as new Note("") in five places, while an
empty interview already has the named constant Interview.NONE.

interview checks, format first and then a real date and time, so
the two copies could drift apart.

Let's add Note.NONE and use it wherever a candidate has no note. Add
Interview.findValidationError, which returns the message for the
first failed check, and use it in both places. This matches how
Email.findValidationError already removes the same duplication for
emails.

Also pass the unchanged note to the edited candidate the same way as
the interview and status, and build the note command's log message
with String.format, as the interview command does.

field on master, so the varied sample data no longer compiles there.

notes and interviews, and give the two UX Designer candidates no

commitResults.messageBody:

repair or move the file themselves. A small editing mistake can
